scope: redirect the decoded 0x66F170 callback to a recording stub and capture its calling contract

session.name: 20261023-stub-5
session.sequence: install counters -> patch 0x66F20E to 90 90 -> write [0x76446B0]=8 -> poll for the rebuilt cl -> read cl2 -> allocate recording stub -> write [cl2+0x30] = stub ^ (cl2+0x2C) ^ [0xE60B78] -> restore 0x66F20E to ff d2 -> wait 0.9 s

retarget.result: the encoded store succeeded, 0x66F20E was restored to ff d2, and the next heartbeat call reached the stub

argument_object.note: only +0x10 (cl2+0x2C) is non-zero: it is the encoded callback that this probe just wrote. The rest of the object is still zero, which is why the shipped decode produced garbage.

out_buffer_before_call.consumer: 0x66F210 mov eax,[ebp-0x14] reads buffer+4; 0x66F216 shr eax,0xC; 0x66F21C and al,1; the result selects the 0x66F231 branch

second_attempt.change: rewrote the same stub to also copy the caller's esi (0x66F170 output structure, 0x2C bytes) and cl2+0x3E4/0x3F8/0x3FC into the record
second_attempt.outcome: record stayed all zero because phase had already fallen back to 0 and cl2 had been re-created (0x1312B3CC with cb30=0), so the heartbeat no longer calls 0x5B2C10
second_attempt.window: the phase-8 window in which the callback can be instrumented lasts roughly one to two seconds after the rebuild

second_probe.sequence: write phase 8 -> wait for rebuilt cl -> read cl2 (0x13150B6C) -> encode [cl2+0x30] -> restore ff d2 -> wait
second_probe.finding: at callback time the message that 0x66F170 is building is still entirely zero, and the three source fields it reads from cl2 are zero as well. The callback therefore is not given an already-built packet; it must itself produce the content that 0x66F210 consumes.

branch_write_attempt.wrong_target: the first probe wrote [eax+4] (cl2+0x20); the consumer actually reads [ecx+4] where ecx is the local 8-byte buffer
branch_write_attempt.correct_target: result+4 of the local buffer passed in ecx
branch_write_attempt.outcome: the window closed before the corrected stub could be hit (phase 0, cl2 re-created to 0x131508F8), so the branch steer is still unmeasured

conclusions: the decoded callback can be redirected precisely by writing [cl2+0x30]; the formula stub ^ (cl2+0x2C) ^ [0xE60B78] is verified by readback and by an actual hit
the callback contract is fn(cl2+0x1C, &local_8byte_result), with edi = cl2+0xC preserved by the caller
the caller only consumes result+4 (bit 12 selects a branch), so a stub can steer the branch by writing that dword
the cl2+0x1C object is entirely uninitialised apart from the encoded callback slot, which is the real structural gap
next: in one phase-8 window: make the stub copy the caller esi (the 0x2C-byte message built by 0x66F170) and cl2+0x3E4/0x3F8/0x3FC into the record before the window closes
then have the stub write result+4 with bit 12 set (0x1000) and observe which 0x5B2C10 branch and whether ring A receives a packet
if the message is the outbound challenge, deliver it through the loopback ring writer 0x6750A0 from the stub or from a follow-up call
